question: What's the trade-off between a fast turn and a slow turn?
choices: Fast: 3 actions, no reaction. Slow: 2 actions plus a reaction
Fast: act before enemies with 2 actions. Slow: act after fast enemies with 3 actions
Fast: 2 actions and disadvantage on attacks. Slow: 3 actions
There's no difference except order
explanation: A fast turn goes before any enemies but gives only two actions; a slow turn comes after fast enemies but gives three. Either way you gain a reaction at the start of your turn.
verify: you only get two actions

question: What's the order of turn phases in a combat round?
choices: Fast PCs, slow PCs, fast NPCs, slow NPCs
Fast NPCs, fast PCs, slow NPCs, slow PCs
Fast PCs, fast NPCs, slow PCs, slow NPCs
Initiative order by d20 roll
explanation: Each round runs: fast PC turns, fast NPC turns, slow PC turns, slow NPC turns, then the next round begins.
verify: Fast NPC Turns
Slow PC Turns

question: When does a character gain reactions in combat?
choices: Only at the start of combat
At the start of combat (unless Surprised) and again at the start of each of their turns
Only on slow turns
At the end of each round
explanation: You gain a reaction when combat starts (unless Surprised), usable before your first turn, then a new one at the start of each of your turns, fast or slow. Each lasts until the start of your next turn or until used.
verify: at the start of each of your turns, you gain a new reaction

question: Can a character use the Strike action more than once per turn?
choices: No, named actions are once per turn
Yes, but each attack must use a different hand, and an offhand attack costs 2 focus
Yes, unlimited times with the same weapon
Only on a slow turn
explanation: Strike is an exception to the once-per-turn rule, but each Strike must use a different hand and attacking with your offhand costs 2 focus.
verify: each attack must use a different hand

question: What does the Brace action do?
choices: Grants +2 deflect until your next turn
Behind cover within 5 feet, attacks against you gain a disadvantage until you attack or move
Lets you ignore the next Shove or Grapple
Makes you immune to being knocked Prone
explanation: Brace puts you behind cover within 5 feet: attacks from the far side of that cover gain a disadvantage until you attack or move. A Defensive-trait weapon like a shield can act as mobile cover.
verify: All attacks against you gain a disadvantage for as long as you stay behind cover

question: What does a successful Gain Advantage action give you?
choices: An advantage on all tests against that enemy this round
An advantage on your next test against that enemy that uses a different skill
An Opportunity on your next test
A free Strike
explanation: After a successful test (a relevant skill vs. the matching defense), you gain an advantage on your next test against that enemy — but it must use a different skill from the one you used to Gain Advantage.
verify: uses a different skill

question: A character is Grappled. Which of these does NOT end the Grapple?
choices: The grappler becomes Unconscious
The target is no longer within the grappler's reach
The grappled character successfully Shoves the grappler
The grappled character takes damage
explanation: Grapple (Athletics vs. Physical) makes the target Restrained until the grappler is Unconscious, chooses to end it, or the target leaves their reach. Successfully Shoving the grappler also ends it. Taking damage doesn't.
verify: it ends the Grapple effect

question: How often can a character use the Recover action, and what does it do?
choices: Once per round; regain 1 focus
Once per scene; roll your recovery die as if you'd finished a short rest
Twice per scene; regain all focus
Unlimited; regain 1d4 health
explanation: Recover (a two-action activity) lets you roll your recovery die for health and/or focus as if after a short rest. It can be used only once per scene.
verify: You can only use the Recover action once per scene

question: What does the Aid reaction cost and give?
choices: Free; +2 to the ally's test
1 focus; the ally gains an advantage on their test
2 focus; the ally rerolls
1 action; the ally gains an Opportunity
explanation: Before an ally makes a skill test, you can use your reaction and spend 1 focus to grant them an advantage — if you're realistically in position to help.
verify: spend 1 focus to grant them an advantage on their test

question: Which statement about the Dodge reaction is correct?
choices: It costs no focus
It adds a disadvantage to an incoming attack for 1 focus, but can't be used against area or multi-target attacks
It lets you move 5 feet out of an area attack
It turns a hit into a graze
explanation: Dodge costs your reaction and 1 focus to add a disadvantage to an attack before it's made. It doesn't work on area attacks or attacks with multiple targets — Avoid Danger might help there.
verify: can’t use this reaction on area attacks

question: What triggers a Reactive Strike, and what does it cost?
choices: An enemy entering your reach; free
An enemy voluntarily leaving your reach; your reaction and 1 focus
Any enemy movement within 30 feet; 1 action
An enemy attacking an ally; 2 focus
explanation: When an enemy voluntarily leaves your reach, you can use your reaction and spend 1 focus to make a melee weapon attack against their Physical defense. Instant movement like Transportation doesn't trigger it.
verify: When an enemy voluntarily leaves your reach

question: An attack misses. What option does the attacker have?
choices: None — a miss deals no damage
Spend 1 focus per target to graze, dealing the damage dice total (no skill modifier)
Spend an Opportunity to hit anyway
Spend 2 focus to reroll
explanation: On a miss you can spend 1 focus per target to graze, dealing damage equal to the damage dice alone. A hit adds your skill modifier to the dice.
verify: spend 1 focus per target of your choice to instead graze them

question: What does turning a hit into a critical hit do?
choices: Doubles all damage
Treats all damage dice as rolling their maximum
Adds one extra damage die
Inflicts an automatic injury
explanation: Spending an Opportunity on a hit makes it a critical hit, maximizing the damage dice against all targets of that attack (the skill modifier is still added as usual).
verify: treat all damage dice as if they rolled their highest number

question: A thrown weapon has range [20/60]. What happens when attacking a target 40 feet away?
choices: Normal attack
The attack gains a disadvantage
The attack can't be made
The attack takes a −5 penalty
explanation: Inside the short range (20 ft) tests are normal; between short and long range (up to 60 ft) they gain a disadvantage; beyond long range you can't attack.

cite.section: Ch. 10 Combat › Long and Short Range

verify: the test gains a disadvantage

question: A PC attacks where they believe a hidden enemy is but can't sense them. What applies?
choices: The attack automatically misses
The attack has a disadvantage and can't graze
Normal attack, but no damage modifier
The attack gains an advantage because the enemy is unaware
explanation: If you know roughly where a target is but can't sense them, attacks and other physical-effect tests against them gain a disadvantage, and those attacks can't graze.

cite.section: Ch. 10 Combat › Locating and Sensing Targets

verify: Attack tests made in this way can’t graze

question: Does forced movement, like a Shove, trigger Reactive Strikes?
choices: Yes, always
No — forced movement doesn't trigger Reactive Strike or other leave-your-reach abilities
Only if the target is pushed more than 5 feet
Only for Large or bigger characters
explanation: Forced movement ignores the target's movement rate and doesn't trigger Reactive Strike or other abilities that trigger when a character leaves your reach.
verify: forced movement doesn’t trigger the Reactive Strike reaction

question: How much falling damage does a character take?
choices: 1d6 impact per 10 feet fallen (from at least 10 feet), and they land Prone if damaged
1d10 per 10 feet, no other effect
1d6 per 5 feet
Flat 5 damage per 10 feet
explanation: Falling at least 10 feet deals 1d6 impact damage per 10 feet. If you take any damage from the fall, you land Prone.
verify: take 1d6 impact damage for every 10 feet you fell

question: What does a rider need to use their mount's abilities (from its stat block) in combat?
choices: Nothing — mounts act on their own turn
A utility expertise in riding that kind of mount (e.g. Riding Horses); the rider spends their own resources
A successful Survival test each round
2 focus per round
explanation: With the right riding expertise you can activate the mount's abilities on your turn using your own focus and actions. Without it, the mount takes no actions of its own.
verify: If you don’t have expertise in riding that mount, they take no actions of their own

question: An ally Shoves an enemy 5 feet, out of the reach of the PC next to it. The PC still has their reaction and focus. Can they make a Reactive Strike?
choices: Yes, it left their reach
Yes, but with a disadvantage
No — forced movement doesn't trigger Reactive Strike
No — Reactive Strike only works on the PC's own turn
explanation: Reactive Strike needs an enemy to voluntarily leave your reach. Being pushed is forced movement, which never triggers it.
verify: Forced movement isn’t affected by that character’s movement rate

question: An enemy Elsecaller standing next to a PC uses Transportation to vanish and reappear across the room. Can the PC Reactive Strike?
choices: Yes, they left reach voluntarily
No — Reactive Strike can't target characters who transport themselves or move instantaneously
Only with an advantage
Only if the PC has a reach weapon
explanation: Reactive Strike explicitly can't be used on a character who transports themselves with Transportation or otherwise moves instantaneously.
verify: transports themself with Transportation

question: A PC archer has an enemy soldier right next to them but shoots at an enemy officer 30 feet away (within short range). What modifies the attack?
choices: Nothing
A disadvantage, because they're within an enemy's reach
An advantage, because the officer is unaware
The stakes are raised
explanation: A ranged attack made while you're within reach of any enemy gains a disadvantage.

cite.section: Ch. 10 Combat › Ranged Attacks and Reach

verify: When you make a ranged attack while you’re within reach of any enemy

question: A PC fires a shortbow at an enemy who is locked in melee, within 5 feet of the PC's ally. The attack misses and the plot die shows a Complication. What can you, the GM, do?
choices: Nothing special — the stakes weren't raised
Spend the Complication to have the attack automatically graze the ally
Make the PC drop their bow
The ally takes full hit damage
explanation: Ranged attacks against a target within 5 feet of the attacker's ally always raise the stakes. On a miss with a Complication, the GM can spend it so the shot grazes the ally, at no focus cost.

cite.section: Ch. 10 Combat › Ranged Attacks and Reach

verify: automatically graze your ally

question: A PC with a +4 Heavy Weaponry modifier hits with a weapon dealing 1d10 keen damage, rolling a 5. The target's armor has deflect 2. How much damage does the target take?
explanation: A hit deals the damage dice plus the skill modifier: 5 + 4 = 9. Keen damage is reduced by deflect: 9 − 2 = 7.
verify: Deal damage equal to the total rolled on the damage dice + your modifier

question: A PC with Light Weaponry +3 attacks with a weapon dealing 2d6, rolls 2 and 4 on the damage dice, and hits. They have an Opportunity and spend it to critically hit. How much damage (before deflect)?
explanation: A critical hit treats all damage dice as their maximum: 2d6 becomes 12. Add the skill modifier for a hit: 12 + 3 = 15.
verify: This maximizes the result of your damage dice

question: A PC's attack misses. Their damage dice rolled a total of 6, and their skill modifier is +3. They spend 1 focus. What happens?
choices: They graze for 6 damage
They graze for 9 damage
They hit for 9 damage
They graze for 3 damage
explanation: Spending 1 focus on a miss turns it into a graze, which deals only the damage dice total — 6 — without the skill modifier.
verify: deal damage equal to the total rolled on the damage dice

question: A PC is shoved off a ledge and falls 30 feet onto stone. What happens?
choices: 1d6 impact damage
3d6 impact damage and they land Prone
3d6 impact damage, no other effect
An automatic injury
explanation: Falling deals 1d6 impact damage per 10 feet — 3d6 for 30 feet — and taking any fall damage leaves you Prone. (They could first try Avoid Danger to catch themselves.)
verify: If you take any damage from a fall, you are Prone when you land

question: A PC uses Gain Advantage, testing Deduction to read a duelist's footwork, and succeeds. Which of their next tests against that duelist can use the advantage?
choices: Any test, including another Deduction test
Their next test against the duelist that uses a different skill, such as a Light Weaponry Strike
Only a Deduction test
Only a test made by an ally
explanation: The advantage applies to your next test against that enemy using a different skill from the one you used to gain it.
verify: use that advantage on your next Light Weaponry test

question: Two PCs have taken fast turns. The third PC planned to go slow but, after seeing the situation, wants to go fast now, before the fast NPCs. Is that allowed?
choices: No — fast/slow must be declared at the start of the round
Yes — the choice can be made in the moment and changes each round
Only if they spend 1 focus
Only with a Speed higher than the other PCs
explanation: You choose fast or slow each round, and the decision doesn't need to be made at the start of the round. You can opt in after the other fast PCs have gone.
verify: your decision doesn’t need to be made at the start of the round

question: Bandits ambush the party, and you rule two PCs are Surprised. What does that mean for those PCs on the first round?
choices: They skip their first turn entirely
No reaction, can't take a fast turn, and one fewer action on their turn; the condition ends after that turn
They have a disadvantage on all tests this round only
They're Prone
explanation: Surprised characters lose reactions (and don't gain one at the start of combat or on their turn), can't take a fast turn, and gain one fewer action. The condition is removed after their next turn.
verify: Remove this condition after your next turn

question: On their turn, a PC uses Ready to Strike the first enemy who comes through a door. No enemy comes through before the PC's next turn. What happens to the actions they spent?
choices: They're refunded on the next turn
They're lost
They carry over as a bonus action
The PC can Strike at any target instead
explanation: If the trigger doesn't occur (or you choose not to respond), you don't regain the actions spent on Ready and the prepared action.
verify: you don’t regain your spent actions

question: An enemy Dustbringer targets an area containing a PC with a gout of flame. The PC wants to Dodge. What's the correct ruling?
choices: Dodge works normally for 1 focus
Dodge can't be used against area attacks; the PC can try Avoid Danger (Agility vs. the attack's test result) instead
The PC automatically takes half damage
Dodge works but costs 2 focus
explanation: Dodge can't be used against area or multi-target attacks. Avoid Danger lets you test Agility against the triggering test's result; on a success you avoid the danger to a reasonable degree, as the GM judges.
verify: the DC is equal to that test’s result

question: A PC is knocked Prone. An enemy swordsman and an enemy archer (30 feet away) both attack them. Which attack gains an advantage from the Prone condition?
choices: Both
Only the swordsman's melee attack
Only the archer's ranged attack
Neither
explanation: While Prone, melee attacks against you gain an advantage. The condition doesn't grant ranged attackers an advantage.
verify: melee attacks against you gain an advantage

question: Playing on a 5-foot grid, a Slowed PC has 5 feet of movement left. Can they move one more square?
choices: Yes — one square costs 5 feet
No — a Slowed character needs at least 10 feet remaining to enter a square
Yes, but only orthogonally
Only with an Athletics test
explanation: On a grid you need at least 5 feet of movement left to enter a square, or 10 feet if you're Slowed.

cite.section: Ch. 10 Combat › Variant: Using a Grid (Movement)

verify: or 10 or more if you are Slowed

question: A PC wants to use an ability that targets 'a character within reach' on themselves. Allowed?
choices: No — abilities target others
Yes — you are a character, so you can target yourself (but you are not your own ally)
Only with GM approval
Only for healing effects
explanation: Since you're a character, an effect targeting 'a character' can target you. Note, though, that you aren't considered your own ally.
verify: you are not considered your ally
